$comment: no-environment: ok — the standard, not a network
title: home.yml — a house, for La Régie (schema 1)
description: The contract every house writes to. Things are data: an id, a room, a kind, how it is reached, and since schema 1 / engine 0.4 what it is FOR (`role`). Packs add fields to a thing (their schema fragment is merged before validation); kinds, via and roles are OPEN vocabularies — an unknown value is a warning, never an error, so a new use case is a pack, not a schema bump. The vocabulary (rooms' scenes, modes, effects, scenarios) is the product's standard library: its shapes live here, `include:` brings them in from small files, the packs render them.

schema.description: the schema version this file is written to; `regie migrate` moves a file forward

name.description: an id for the house (paths, topics)

url.description: the brain's URL for the phones (internal and external are the same door)

my.description: My Home Assistant (my.home-assistant.io): true = Home Assistant's default, every OAuth consent redirects through the project's page; false = the brain's own door is the callback (<url>/auth/external/callback - what a vendor's app registers) and default_config is rendered explicitly without `my`

profile.description: where the brain runs: a folder under profiles/ (ct, and later pi, vm, docker)

packs.description: the use cases enabled: product packs (packs/) and the house's own (paths.house_packs)

root.description: the brain's tree on its host; the profile's default otherwise

house_packs.description: a directory of the house's own packs, relative to home.yml

units_dir.description: where the host's units go (`regie up`); the profile's default otherwise

owner.description: the brain's own owner account — the break-glass login that needs no provider; its password is the secret `owner_password`. Created by `regie apply` at the first boot (Home Assistant's onboarding), never by a person at a screen.

backup.description: Home Assistant's own backup, scheduled by `regie apply` (encrypted with the secret `backup_password`)

time.description: local time of the nightly backup

tokens.description: long-lived access tokens the house's own machines need (a scraper, an automation that calls the API) — minted once by `regie apply`, kept root-only under <root>/.regie/tokens/<name>, never printed

floors.description: the floors the areas name (optional: a floor an area names without a line here is created with its id as its name)

pins.description: the images' tags; the profile carries the versions this release was tested against, a house may override (doctor says so)

proxy.description: a reverse proxy in front of the brain (optional)

trusted.description: its addresses or networks (X-Forwarded-For is trusted from these)

via.description: the proxy's address the brain proves its door through before promoting the HTTP config (default: the one trusted proxy when it is a single host) - on the brain the door's name may resolve to the brain itself

oidc.description: an OpenID Connect door (optional — without it, Home Assistant's own login). The client secret is the secret `oidc_client_secret`.

admin.description: the provider's group that makes an admin

user.description: the provider's group that lets a person in

features.description: the component's `features:` block, passed as is (automatic_person_creation, include_groups_scope, default_redirect, ...)

claims.description: the component's `claims:` block, passed as is (display_name, username, groups)

channel.description: fixed before the first pairing; changing it re-pairs the mesh

host.description: where the things reach the broker; the brain itself uses the loopback

include.description: small files merged into this one before validation — an engine feature, the same on a Pi and on a fleet. Paths and globs are relative to home.yml. rooms: one file per room, merged into the area of the same id (created when `areas:` has no line for it); modes / fx: exactly one file each, in place of the block here; scenarios: one story per file (its id = the file's stem unless the file says `id:`)

scenarios.description: the stories — steps, waits, effects, scenes, words; one file each under include.scenarios

level.description: 0 = the ground floor; the UI sorts by it

aliases.description: what people SAY for this room (pushed to Home Assistant's area aliases beside the id; the voice pipeline matches on them)

roles.description: the roles this room has — what a thing is FOR here (lights: main · accent · lamp · strip · night · shelf · console…; the rest: remote · motion · door · screen · speaker · satellite…). An open enumeration; the walk fills them (`role:` on a thing's row)

scenes.description: the room's looks by role; each renders as a script <room>_<scene> once a role it names is filled. `off` is implicit: every filled role off

defaults.description: per period (the keys of modes.periods): the scene "on" means then — a scene id, or one per daylight (dark / dim / bright). sensor.<room>_default carries it; every turn-on path applies it

behaviours.description: the packs' behaviour templates with this room's knobs — each pack documents its own keys (0.4: a seam, nothing reads it yet)

phone.description: the companion app's notify slug (notify.mobile_app_<phone>) — makes the person a target of the mouth (notify.<person>, notify.household)

coordinator.description: one Zigbee radio = one Zigbee2MQTT instance; reached over TCP. Its address comes from the thing it names (kind: coordinator) or from `host`.

thing.description: the thing (kind: coordinator) whose `host` is the radio's address

host.description: the radio's address, when it is not a thing

adapter.description: zstack (TI CC26x2), ember (Silicon Labs), deconz, zigate, zboss

base_topic.description: the instance's MQTT root; `zigbee2mqtt` for the first coordinator, `zigbee2mqtt_<id>` for the others

id.description: one name, three systems: the Zigbee2MQTT friendly name, the MQTT topic, the entity's object id

kind.description: what it is (x-known.kinds + the packs'); open

via.description: how it is reached (x-known.via + the packs'); open

label.description: the family's word for this one; the kind's label otherwise

ieee.description: a Zigbee thing's address — filled by the pairing walk

coordinator.description: the radio a Zigbee thing is on; the first coordinator otherwise

mac.description: a network thing's hardware address (a reservation, a row)

entity.description: the entity id when it cannot be derived from the kind and the id

integration.description: the Home Assistant integration(s) that reach it — one config entry each (the conductor's business); a list when one box is several things to Home Assistant (a receiver: heos + denonavr; a TV: androidtv_remote + cast)

bind.description: a control bound inside the mesh to things or areas (an area = its Zigbee group)

options.description: what a pack reads on a thing of its kinds; each pack documents its own

role.description: what the thing is FOR in its room (main, accent, lamp, strip, night, shelf, console, remote, motion, door, screen, speaker, satellite…) — the key scenes and effects are written on, before the walk; open

at.description: its place in the role's layout (front_left, row_3…) — needs a role; the walk assigns it

aliases.description: what people say for this one

look.description: what a role looks like in a scene: on / off, or a mapping — brightness (0-100), ct (warm | neutral | cool | kelvin), color (#rrggbb), transition (seconds)

scene.description: a persistent look for the room, BY ROLE — no entity id anywhere; a role nothing fills yet renders nothing

role.description: what a room expects for one of its roles — a label, and for a ceiling of many lights its layout (the places the walk assigns with `at:`)

layout.description: the places, in order (front_left, front_center, …, row_1, …): places sharing a prefix make a group of their own (light.<room>_<role>_<prefix>); effects sweep in this order

daylight_map.description: a scene per daylight (the signal sensor.daylight: dark below the horizon, dim at low sun, bright)

quiet.description: the mouth stays silent in this mode unless the severity is alarm (binary_sensor.house_quiet)

scene.description: the scene every room takes when the house enters this mode: a scene id, `default` (the room's default for the period), or `off`

else.description: the scene a room takes when it lacks the one above (off, for instance)

rooms.description: per room, a scene instead of the mode's

away.description: the house is empty in this mode (binary_sensor.house_occupied reads off)

to.description: the mode the house enters when this period begins

from.description: only when the house is in one of these modes (a cinema at 22:30 is not interrupted); any mode when absent

modes.description: the house's state machine: input_select.house_mode, one automation per transition, the periods (four times editable in the UI, seeded from here once), the clock rules and the daylight thresholds

initial.description: the mode the brain starts in the very first time (seeded once by the conductor; the UI's choice is kept after)

periods.description: in order of the day — each begins at its time (an input_datetime the family edits in the UI; this file only seeds it); before the first, the last one holds (night wraps)

clock.description: per period: the mode its beginning moves the house to

dark_below.description: the sun's elevation (degrees) under which it is dark (civil twilight = -6)

follow.description: when the period or the daylight changes and the house is in a mode whose scene is `default`, the rooms that are lit take their new default

shape.description: an effect's SHAPE — what, never how: steps of level / colour / hold / transition, repeats, bricks composed (`use:`); a backend compiles it at the protocol's resolution

step.description: the finest hold it asks for, seconds

fields.description: the shape's knobs with their defaults — the script's fields; a step refers to one as $name

repeat.description: how many times the steps run ($times, or a number)

fx.description: which effects the house enables, on which backend, its own shapes

backend.description: the compiler every target goes through at 0.4 (ha: the generic light-service loop); per-protocol backends land with their bench

enable.description: the shapes rendered as scripts; every shape when absent

shapes.description: the house's own shapes, beside the product's

kelvin.description: what warm / neutral / cool mean in a scene (2700 / 4000 / 5500 by default)

scenario_step.description: one step of a story: a mode, a scene (room/scene), an effect, a wait, words

period.description: when a period begins: a time (HH:MM), or {at, label} — the label is what the family sees on the time helper

scene_ref.description: a scene id — `off` (YAML reads a bare off as false: both are taken) or `default`
